display.purpose: Hero and section titles only. Blunt idiosyncratic grotesque (Bricolage Grotesque); big, heavy, and rare. The hero wordmark is a static WebP lit like a light box (mix-blend: screen + a CSS turn-on/flicker glow); the accessible <h1> wraps it.

headline.purpose: Sub-section heads in docs and long pages. Public Sans 700.

title.purpose: Card titles, callout heads, the strong line above a paragraph.

body.purpose: Prose and docs, site-wide at 1.125rem (--xrw-text-md); base line-height 1.5, long-form prose opts to 1.6. Code blocks pin to 1rem (--xrw-text-base). 65–75ch measure.

label.purpose: Machine voice only — filenames, plate names, coverage bands, kbd hints. JetBrains Mono.

fonts.loader: Astro Fonts API (fontProviders.fontsource()), self-hosted + preloaded, with automatic metric-matched fallbacks (size-adjust / ascent-override) for zero font-swap CLS. Exposed as --xrw-font-display / -body / -mono.

shadows.name: backlight-ambient
shadows.purpose: Resting steel glow behind primary actions, boxes, and the active nav item. Diffuse bloom, no offset. Pairs with an inset pass for backlit film edges.

shadows.name: backlight-inset
shadows.purpose: Inner glow on cards/asides/code frames — lit from within as well as without.

shadows.name: backlight-focus
shadows.purpose: Focus ring — a single 2px solid steel outline at 3px offset (was a double ring), visible in both themes, never removed.

shadows.name: exposure-hover
shadows.purpose: Bone-white bloom on hover for cards/tiles — the element brightens as if pulled toward the light.

motion.name: ease-out-quint
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions and reveals. Exponential ease-out, no bounce.

motion.name: duration-expose
motion.purpose: The capture-flash bloom and the skeleton→content exposure reveal.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Mandatory fallback: the flash becomes a single quiet crossfade, sibling-stagger reveals resolve instantly, the demo's auto-cue and nav slide are skipped.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The lit element on the page — reserved for a single exceptionally important CTA, never the default (ghost is the default). On hover the edge lights with a wider backlit glow; no 1px lift. Text uses the film black, not pure #000.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: oklch(0.62 0.11 246); color: oklch(0.09 0.02 256); font: 500 0.9375rem/1 'Public Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 12px 24px; border: none; border-radius: 3px; cursor: pointer; transition: box-shadow 160ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { box-shadow: 0 0 24px -6px oklch(0.62 0.11 246 / 0.55); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(0.62 0.11 246); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The default CTA (the site's lead actions are all this variant). Hairline border lights to steel with a backlit glow on hover, struck on with a quick flicker site-wide.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: oklch(0.62 0.11 246); font: 500 0.9375rem/1 'Public Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 12px 24px; border: 1px solid oklch(0.28 0.02 253); border-radius: 3px; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), box-shadow 160ms; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: oklch(0.62 0.11 246); box-shadow: 0 0 14px -3px oklch(0.62 0.11 246 / 0.5); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(0.62 0.11 246); outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview: A darkened radiology reading room. A film hangs on the negatoscope and glows from behind; the bones read as luminous blue-white against the black. xray captures the real skeleton of a UI and renders it faithfully, so the brand feels like reading a radiograph: clinical, exact, quietly luminous, and faintly unnerving. Playful, with a hint of doom. There is one palette: dark is the positive radiograph (backlit film in the reading room, the hero mood); light is that exact page inverted — a photographic negative (invert(1) hue-rotate(180deg), raster media re-inverted). System-driven, no toggle.
keyCharacteristics: One palette; dark is the positive radiograph, light is the page inverted. No toggle.
A narrow three-hue cast (~250): cool film-blue, a desaturated steel accent, rare crimson.
A page-wide film filter (grain, vignette, glow) — no scroll-repainting blend or backdrop-filter; the tone curve lives in the deepened palette.
Depth is conveyed by glow (text + box, inward and outward), never grey drop shadows.
A blunt idiosyncratic grotesque (Bricolage Grotesque) over clinical institutional sans (Public Sans), self-hosted via the Astro Fonts API with zero font-swap CLS.
The site dogfoods xray's own skeletons as its real loading states (pending; today the hero comparison slider is the live capture demo).

rules.name: The Three-Hue Rule
rules.body: The entire system is one cool blue-grey neutral plus radiograph-steel plus contrast-crimson. No fourth hue earns its way in. Breadth comes from luminance and the bones, not from more colors.

rules.name: The Bloodless Rule
rules.body: Contrast-crimson appears on a vanishingly small fraction of any view. A hint of gore is unnerving; gore everywhere is a horror-movie poster. If crimson is the first color you notice, it has overstayed.

rules.name: The Negative Rule
rules.body: There is one palette: the dark film. Light mode is that exact page inverted (invert(1) hue-rotate(180deg)), never a separately-tuned light theme. Raster media (img, video, canvas) is re-inverted so photos read normally.

rules.name: The Blunt-Not-Tasteful Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque is here for its wonk and bluntness, not polish. Use it big and heavy; never tracked out, never italic over ruled columns (the editorial-magazine lane this brand rejects). The hint of doom rides on the palette (rare crimson), the deadpan doctor mark, the dark reading-room mood, and a fine film-grain texture — not on the type.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Machine Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for things the computer produced or consumes — code, filenames, plate names, coverage states, shortcuts. Prose is never mono.

rules.name: The No-Shift Rule
rules.body: All three families are self-hosted and preloaded through the Astro Fonts API (fontProviders.fontsource()), each with an automatic metric-matched fallback (size-adjust / ascent-override) so the swap causes zero layout shift. Plain @fontsource CSS imports, which reflow on swap, are forbidden.

rules.name: The Backlight Rule
rules.body: Depth is light, not shadow. Every elevation is a glow that brightens toward steel or bone-white; offset grey drop shadows are prohibited, and the 1px-border-plus-soft-grey-drop-shadow ghost card is doubly banned. The page-wide film uses no blend mode or backdrop-filter (they repaint on scroll); the tone curve lives in the palette.

rules.name: The Dogfood Rule
rules.body: Loading and empty states on this site are real xray skeletons, not hand-drawn placeholders. The site is the demo.

dos: Do follow the system theme with no toggle; light mode is the dark film inverted (the Negative Rule), not a separately-tuned theme.
Do hold the palette to the Three-Hue Rule: one cool film-blue neutral, Radiograph Steel, and a rare Contrast Crimson.
Do keep Contrast Crimson rare (the Bloodless Rule) — danger and the macabre wink only.
Do convey depth with the steel/bone glow and the page-wide film filter (the Backlight Rule); flat at rest.
Do dogfood xray's own skeletons as the site's real loading states (the Dogfood Rule) — pending; the hero comparison slider is the current live capture demo.
Do pair every color-coded state with text, icon, or shape — never color alone (WCAG 2.2 AA).
Do give every motion — capture flash, exposure reveal, sibling-stagger entrances — a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce crossfade-or-instant fallback.
Do load fonts via the Astro Fonts API with metric-matched fallbacks (the No-Shift Rule); keep body measure at 65–75ch.
donts: Don't ship the generic dev-tool SaaS look: the Vercel/Linear clean-dark-gradient clone, the hero-metric template, the glow-blob background.
Don't drift into editorial-magazine: display-serif italic, ruled multi-column layouts, lowercase track-spaced mono eyebrows above every section.
Don't go cutesy / mascot-heavy: no hand-drawn doodles, sketchy feTurbulence SVGs, or sticker energy. The doctor mark is a deadpan caricature.
Don't go enterprise / corporate: no stock-photo teams, trust badges, or endless grids of identical icon-heading-text feature cards.
Don't use grey offset drop shadows, or the 1px-border + ≥16px-blur ghost card. Depth is light here.
Don't round cards past 8px, use colored side-stripe borders, gradient text, default glassmorphism, or repeating-stripe backgrounds.
Don't set body copy in mono or all-caps; mono means the machine is talking.
